name: bounty-radar
description: Zero-dependency Node.js toolkit that sweeps Algora, Opire and GitHub for open-source bounties, jobs and challenges, verifies repo liveness via the GitHub CLI, filters spam and ranks results. Publishes HTML/RSS/JSON and exposes an MCP server for AI agents.

paragraphs: Sweep, verify and rank open-source bounties, jobs and challenges.

Bounty Radar is a zero-dependency Node.js toolkit that collects open-source bounty listings, checks that the repository behind each one is still alive, filters known spam patterns, and ranks what is left with a simple, explainable score. The same feed is published as a static HTML board, RSS and JSON, and exposed to AI coding agents through an MCP server.
features: Six collectors in radar.mjs: Algora org bounty pages, Algora jobs pages, Algora challenges, GitHub issues that mention @algora-io, Opire rewards found via GitHub search, and GitHub issues carrying common bounty labels.

Liveness verification through the GitHub CLI: drops archived repos, bounties on forks (for label-sourced issues), repos not pushed within 60 days and issues that are no longer open; counts open PRs that compete for the…
Spam and bait filtering: regex blocklist for known fake-bounty repos/orgs and a filter for the copy-pasted [Bounty: $X] title template.
Deterministic scoring: points for amount, freshness, claim count, competing PRs and recent repo activity; duplicates are merged keeping the highest amount.
Outputs: Markdown digest, JSON (--json), and a static site (build-site.mjs) with index.html, feed.xml (RSS 2.0) and bounties.json.

whatItDoes.text: Sweep, verify and rank open-source bounties, jobs and challenges.

requirements.text: Optional API (worker/): a Cloudflare Worker serving /v1/listings, /v1/diff, /v1/sources, /v1/stats and an OpenAPI document, with KV-backed API keys and per-IP rate limits.
